import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Check if any feature shows significant association with outcome
    # using Welch's t-test
    p_values = []
    feature_ids = feats.ids
    
    for i, fid in enumerate(feature_ids):
        col = feats.column(fid)
        x = feats.x[:, col]
        y = feats.y
        
        # Welch's t-test
        t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(x[y == 0], x[y == 1], equal_var=False)
        p_values.append(p_val)
    
    # If all p-values > 0.05, no mechanism
    if all(p > 0.05 for p in p_values):
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Find top features by p-value (most significant)
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(p_values)
    top_features = [feature_ids[i] for i in sorted_indices[:10]]
    
    # Check for correlations among top features to remove near-duplicates
    corr_threshold = 0.6
    correlated_pairs = set()
    
    # Build correlation matrix
    col_indices = [feats.column(fid) for fid in top_features]
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, col_indices].T)
    
    # Identify correlated pairs
    for i in range(len(top_features)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(top_features)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i, j]) >= corr_threshold:
                fid1, fid2 = top_features[i], top_features[j]
                # Keep the one with better p-value
                idx1 = feature_ids.index(fid1)
                idx2 = feature_ids.index(fid2)
                if p_values[idx1] < p_values[idx2]:
                    correlated_pairs.add((fid1, fid2))
                else:
                    correlated_pairs.add((fid2, fid1))
    
    # Remove correlated features (keep only one from each pair)
    selected_features = set(top_features)
    for fid1, fid2 in correlated_pairs:
        if fid1 in selected_features and fid2 in selected_features:
            # Remove the one with higher p-value
            idx1 = feature_ids.index(fid1)
            idx2 = feature_ids.index(fid2)
            if p_values[idx1] > p_values[idx2]:
                selected_features.remove(fid1)
            else:
                selected_features.remove(fid2)
    
    # For stratified analysis, check consistency across strata
    strata = list(set(feats.stratum))
    if len(strata) > 1:
        strata_pvals = defaultdict(list)
        for s in strata:
            mask = [i for i, label in enumerate(feats.stratum) if label == s]
            s_x = feats.x[mask]
            s_y = feats.y[mask]
            
            for i, fid in enumerate(feature_ids):
                col = feats.column(fid)
                x = s_x[:, col]
                t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(x[s_y == 0], x[s_y == 1], equal_var=False)
                strata_pvals[fid].append(p_val)
        
        # Filter features that show consistent significance across strata
        filtered_features = []
        for fid in selected_features:
            pvals = strata_pvals[fid]
            if all(p < 0.05 for p in pvals):
                filtered_features.append(fid)
        selected_features = set(filtered_features)
    
    # Final selection: use top features that pass both tests
    final_features = list(selected_features)[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    # Return empty design if no strong signal
    if not final_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Use top features for regression
    columns = tuple(final_features)
    
    # Try adding interaction terms for top 2 features
    products = ()
    if len(final_features) >= 2:
        products = ((final_features[0], final_features[1]),)
    
    # Create a weighted score from top features
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(final_features):
        loadings[fid] = 1.0 / len(final_features)  # Equal weights
    
    # Select drivers based on statistical significance
    drivers = tuple(final_features)
    
    # Ensure we don't exceed MAX_DRIVERS
    if len(drivers) > MAX_DRIVERS:
        drivers = drivers[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
